question: Six 6-sided dice are rolled.  What is the probability that the number of dice showing even numbers and the number of dice showing odd numbers is equal?
solution:
Equal counts require exactly three even dice and three odd dice. Each die has three even and three odd faces, so either parity has probability \(1/2\). By independence, each specific parity pattern has probability \((1/2)^6=1/64\). There are \(\binom{6}{3}=(6\cdot5\cdot4)/(3\cdot2\cdot1)=20\) ways to choose the three even dice. Thus the probability is \(20/64=5/16\).
Final answer: \frac{5}{16}
